name: Samaria Gorge
seoTitle: Samaria Gorge: Length, Entrance Fee, Season and Hiking Time
seoDescription: Samaria Gorge is a 16 km one-way hike from Xyloskalo at 1,250 m down to Agia Roumeli. It takes 5-7 hours, costs 10 EUR to enter and opens 1 May to 31 October.
summary: Samaria Gorge is a 16 km hike through a national park in western Crete, running one way from Xyloskalo on the Omalos Plateau at about 1,250 metres down to the coastal village of Agia Roumeli on the Libyan Sea. The average walker takes 5 to 7 hours; entry costs 10 EUR and the gorge is typically open from 1 May to 31 October. It is the longest gorge walk in Europe that most visitors will attempt, and its narrowest point, Sideroportes or the Iron Gates, closes to a few metres across with cliffs rising almost vertically several hundred metres overhead. Agia Roumeli has no road, so the day always ends with a ferry.
body:
## The hike

The walk starts at Xyloskalo, the northern gate of Samaria Gorge National Park on the Omalos Plateau, at around 1,250 metres. Xyloskalo means wooden staircase and the name is earned in the first hour: stone steps and rocky ground cut into the mountainside, cool air, wide views over the White Mountains, and a descent that is hard on the knees.

Lower down the trail levels out at the abandoned village of Samaria, the midpoint and the natural place to rest. Stone houses, the church of Osia Maria and the remains of village life mark a community that lived here year-round until the area became a national park.

Below the village the path drops into the riverbed proper. The walls rise and close in, boulders block the line, and at Sideroportes, the Iron Gates, the gorge narrows to a few metres while the cliffs go up almost vertically for several hundred metres. After that the terrain flattens, the vegetation thins and the route runs down to sea level and the southern checkpoint.

## Agia Roumeli and the ferry

The hike ends at Agia Roumeli, a village on the Libyan Sea reachable only on foot or by boat. There is time to swim and eat before the ferry to Chora Sfakion, from where the road home begins. Missing the boat is the one genuine failure mode of the day, which is why guided groups track their pace against it.

## Season and fee

The park is normally open 1 May to 31 October. Entry is 10 EUR per adult, paid at the gate, and the ferry ticket is separate. Outside the season the full route is closed, though a short stretch from Agia Roumeli sometimes stays walkable.

## Is it hard?

Medium to high. The difficulty is length and relentless downhill rather than exposure or scrambling, and knees rather than lungs do the suffering. It is not recommended for people with heart conditions or serious knee problems. May and September give the best walking temperatures.

faqs.q: How long does the Samaria Gorge hike take?
faqs.a: The average hiker completes the 16 km trail in 5 to 7 hours. A full day from Rethymno, including the drive to Omalos, the walk, the ferry from Agia Roumeli and the return, runs about 12 hours.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to enter Samaria Gorge?
faqs.a: 10 EUR per adult, paid at the entrance. The ferry from Agia Roumeli to Chora Sfakion is a separate ticket.
Typically from 1 May to 31 October. Dates shift slightly year to year with the weather, and the park closes the trail after heavy rain.

It is a medium-to-high difficulty walk. There is no climbing and no exposure, but 16 km of continuous descent puts real strain on the knees. It is not recommended for anyone with heart conditions or significant knee problems.

faqs.q: Can you walk part of Samaria Gorge?
faqs.a: Yes. The short version, sometimes called Samaria the lazy way, starts at Agia Roumeli and walks up to the Iron Gates and back. It is roughly 6 km return and reaches the most dramatic section without committing to the full descent.
